senses.gloss: <he>כֹּהֵן מ׳</he> or <he>מ׳</he> (v. <cite ref="M02822"><he>מָשׁוּחַ</he></cite>, s. v. <cite ref="M02846"><he>מָשַׁח</he> I</cite>, v.
units: Lev. IV, 3) the high priest installed by anointment.

<cite ref="Tosefta Megillah 1:18">Tosef. Meg. I, 18</cite> <he>כ׳ מ׳ משמש</he> the active high priest; <he>כ׳ מ׳ שעבר</he> the unfitted high priest (prevented from officiating on the Day of Atonement).

Hor. III, 4 ואיזהו המ׳ המשוח וכ׳ what high priest is called mashiaḥ? He who has been anointed &c. Sifra Vayikra, Ḥobah, ch. I, Par. 2, a. e. מ׳ יכול זה המלך by mashiaḥ (Lev. IV, 3) you might understand the king.
<cite ref="Leviticus 4:3">Ib.</cite> <he>המ׳ זה מ׳ וכ׳</he> ‘the anointed’ means an anointed who has no superior anointed; a. fr.

senses.gloss: מֶלֶךְ הַמָּ׳, or מָ׳ the Messiah, the future redeemer of Israel from captivity.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 2:4">Gen. R. s. 2</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 1:2">Gen. I, 2</cite>) <he>זה רוחו של מ׳ המ׳</he> that means the divine spirit of the king Messiah (with ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 11:2">Is. XI, 2</cite>).
<cite ref="Sukkah 52a:2">Succ. 52ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>מ׳ בן דוד</he> the Davidic Messiah, contrad. to <he>מ׳ בן יוסף</he> the M., son of Joseph, who is to precede the former.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 98b:12">Snh. 98ᵇ</cite> <he>אין מ׳ לישראל וכ׳</he> Israel has no Messiah to expect, for it has enjoyed him (the glory which he was predicted to bring) in the days of Hezekiah.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 97a:11">Ib. 97ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.—<he>ימות המ׳</he> the Messianic epoch.

<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 1:5">Ber. I, 5</cite> <he>להביא לימות מ׳</he> this includes (the duty of remembering the exodus from Egypt) even in the Messianic days; a. fr.—<he>חבלו של מ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="H00088"><he>חֵבֶל</he></cite>.—Pl. <he>מְשִׁיחִים</he>.

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 8:1">Pesik. R. s. 8</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Zechariah 4:3">Zech. IV, 3</cite>) <he>אלו שני המ׳ אחד משוח מלחמה וכ׳</he> these are the two expected Messiahs, one appointed to conduct war (<he>מ׳ בן יוסף</he>) &c.; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 570:4">Yalk. Zech. 570</cite>.
